lecture: فلسفهٔ سیاسی با تکیه بر لیبرالیسم (جلسهٔ پنجم، بخش اول؛ جلسهٔ هفتم، بخش دوم)
speaker: Sabouri, D.
summary_of_lecture_fa: این فایل دو تکه است. در تکهٔ اول سخنران بحث جان لاک را کامل می‌کند: حکومت بر پایهٔ رضایت، تفاوت غلبه و غصب و ستمگری، حق مردم برای برکناری حکومت، و جدایی دین از دولت. در تکهٔ دوم، کتاب «دربارهٔ آزادی» و «انقیاد زنان» از جان استوارت میل را می‌خواند و شرح می‌دهد. سخنران در کل از سنت لیبرال دفاع می‌کند و گاهی آن را به تاریخ ایران وصل می‌کند؛ این اتصال‌ها دیدگاه خود اوست و محل بحث است.

quality_notes: The file contains two lecture parts: (1) session 5 part 1, a recap of Locke plus a long Q&A, with the planned Montesquieu material not reached in this part; (2) session 7 part 2, Mill's On Liberty and The Subjection of Women, ending with a preview of von Mises and Adam Smith. ASR is noisy (names and numbers garbled; some page numbers uncertain). Page numbers and Persian translation quotations were not reproduced. Large Q&A stretches on Iranian politics (1979 revolution, Pahlavi development, referendum speculation, Taliban, Afghanistan) were left out as current-events punditry; only the cultural-change-and-ritual point was used. Not verified or omitted: the Kuwait parliament anecdote (sheep slaughtered for MPs); the claim that Marx wrote about women's oppression in the censorship essay (stated from memory by the lecturer); the Soviet-Central Asia cultural-erasure example. Note for editors: Hobbes did allow a right of self-defence against the sovereign, which the lecturer did not mention; the Locke entry therefore does not repeat the lecturer's blanket claim that Hobbes denied any right to resist. Source years for Locke (1689/1690) and Hume (1748) are the first-publication dates as commonly cited.
